title: Which way does each row go, and by how much?
description: Joseph reads two rows on a tally board at a grain market in Nagpur, one falling and one rising. The video finds each rule and fills the blanks.
teaching_notes: One idea: first see whether the row goes up or down, then use the whole gap. Watch for children who round the gap to a thousand.

source: Let Us Do 1 (h), (i), continue the patterns
video_script.why: The child can find a rule that adds or takes away and now meets a falling row whose gap is not a round number.
video_script.substitution: Check if the row rises or falls, find the whole gap between neighbours, and use it to fill the blanks.
video_script.anchor: a tally board at the grain market in Nagpur that Joseph reads
video_script.wrong_move: Chintu sees that the first row falls by about one thousand and says the rule is take away one thousand. The real gap is one thousand one.
video_script.payoff_line: the rule is take away one thousand one

final_answer.spoken: take away one thousand one, then add one thousand

never_show: the answer rows before the idea part
maths_rules: slip: take away 1,000 gives 73,005 − 1,000 = 72,005, but the row has 72,004
video_script.design: Exercise: one falling and one rising row. Hint: check the direction, then the whole gap. Two rows sit on the stage; the gaps arrive as labels in the idea part.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='story'/>Joseph reads two rows of numbers on a tally board at the grain market in Nagpur.
<bookmark mark='one'/>The first row goes seventy three thousand five, then seventy two thousand four, and two blanks.
<bookmark mark='two'/>The second row starts with eighty two thousand three hundred fifty. Next comes eighty three thousand three hundred fifty, and then two blanks.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Continue both rows.

narration: [chintu] <bookmark mark='chintu'/>The first row falls by about one thousand, so the rule is take away one thousand.
<bookmark mark='test'/>Test it on the first jump. Seventy three thousand five take away one thousand is seventy two thousand five.
<bookmark mark='strike'/>That does not match the row, which has seventy two thousand four.

beats.on_screen: the first row gets the board line 73,005 − 72,004 = 1,001 and the rule card subtract 1,001; the blanks fill with 71,003 and 70,002
narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>Seventy three thousand five take away seventy two thousand four leaves one thousand one.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The row falls by one thousand one every time, so the rule is take away one thousand one.
<bookmark mark='one'/>Seventy two thousand four take away one thousand one is seventy one thousand three.
<bookmark mark='two'/>Take away one thousand one again to reach seventy thousand two.

beats.on_screen: the second row gets the board line 83,350 − 82,350 = 1,000 and the rule card add 1,000; the blanks fill with 84,350 and 85,350

<bookmark mark='gap'/>Eighty three thousand three hundred fifty take away eighty two thousand three hundred fifty leaves one thousand.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>The rule is add one thousand.
<bookmark mark='fill'/>Add one thousand to reach eighty four thousand three hundred fifty, then eighty five thousand three hundred fifty.
